lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your situation.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child I'm asking about - my son Alex. He's 6 years old and lives with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex. Now I need to understand more about your living situation and residency status.

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK. I'm currently living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since you're living abroad, there are specific circumstances where you might still be eligible for Child Benefit.

**Can you tell me which country you're currently living in, and are you a Crown servant (such as a diplomat or member of the armed forces posted overseas)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not a Crown servant - I'm not in the military or working as a diplomat or anything like that. I'm just living abroad with my family.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Since you're living abroad and are not a Crown servant, I need to understand a bit more about your situation.

**Are you living in an EU/EEA country or Switzerland, or are you living somewhere else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not get into all those specifics about exactly where I am right now. Does it really matter for the eligibility?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, I'm afraid it does matter significantly for eligibility. The rules for Child Benefit when living abroad are quite specific.

Generally, Child Benefit is available to people who live in the UK. There are only very limited exceptions for people living abroad, which include:

- Being a Crown servant (which you've confirmed you're not)
- Living in certain specific countries under particular circumstances (such as EU/EEA countries or Switzerland with certain conditions)

Without knowing where you're living and the specific circumstances of your situation abroad, I cannot determine whether any exceptions might apply to you.

**Are you able to tell me whether you're in an EU/EEA country, Switzerland, or elsewhere? This is essential information to assess your eligibility.**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm living outside of Europe - not in an EU or EEA country or Switzerland.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Based on what you've told me, I now have enough information to assess your eligibility.

Let me summarize your situation:
- You have one child, Alex, aged 6, living with you
- You live abroad (outside the UK)
- You are not in an EU/EEA country or Switzerland
- You are not a Crown servant

According to the Child Benefit rules, you normally need to live in the UK to qualify for Child Benefit. The main exceptions for people living abroad are:

1. Being a Crown servant (diplomat, armed forces member, etc.)
2. Living in certain countries (EU/EEA or Switzerland) under specific circumstances

Since you don't fall into either of these categories, you would not be eligible for UK Child Benefit while living outside the UK in your current circumstances.

**Unfortunately, you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

The key issue is that you do not meet the residency requirement. To qualify for Child Benefit, you normally need to live in the UK. Since you're living abroad outside of the UK in a non-EU/EEA country and you're not a Crown servant, you don't fall into any of the exceptions that would allow you to claim Child Benefit while living abroad.

If your circumstances change in the future - for example, if you move back to the UK - you would be able to claim Child Benefit at that time for Alex (as long as he's still under 16, or under 20 if in approved education or training).
